headline: Arkansas defense suffocates Michigan in road win despite turnover trouble
body: Arkansas walked out of Ann Arbor with a 34-16 victory that looked more dominant than the yardage totals suggest. K.J. Jackson orchestrated an efficient passing attack that leaned on vertical shots downfield, completing 20 of 39 attempts for 313 yards and two touchdowns. The difference wasn't volume—Michigan's Browne actually threw for 344 yards—but rather timing and field position. Arkansas methodically converted Michigan mistakes into points, and when the Razorbacks needed a stop, their defense delivered.

The turning point arrived in the third quarter when Arkansas's defensive line, anchored by Worth Jr's relentless pursuit, forced Michigan into consecutive negative plays. Worth Jr's two sacks dismantled drive momentum at critical junctures, and while the box score may not fully capture it, Michigan's run game—bottled up at 83 yards—never found rhythm. Browne was forced into uncomfortable situations, checking down more often than attacking vertically. Meanwhile, Parker's vertical catches for Arkansas, particularly his 121-yard day on six receptions including a touchdown, punished Michigan's secondary when it sat too shallow.

Arkansas surrendered two fumbles yet still dictated the tempo and outcome. The coaching room's decision to commit to light box coverage, trusting the pass rush to generate pressure, proved shrewd against Michigan's run-first mentality. Burkett's 10 carries netted only 45 yards—a damning indictment of how thoroughly the Razorback front seven took that phase away. When Michigan tried to establish anything sustained, Arkansas reset and reset again.
turningPoint: Worth Jr's two sacks in the third quarter collapsed Michigan's offensive rhythm and shifted field position decisively in Arkansas's favor, turning a close game into a runaway.

unsungHero.name: Worth Jr
unsungHero.why: Jackson earned Player of the Game, but Worth Jr's two sacks and relentless edge pressure were the foundational reason Michigan never sustained drives or built scoring momentum—defensive dominance doesn't always get headlines.
